What’s new in the W3C Website Design System? Find out at this post by Nicola Saunders, Front-End Lead Developer at Studio 24.

Changes include replacing an old CSS reset, rebuilding typography around a new type scale, reviewing how space is managed, and removing several wrapper elements to simplify page markup.

See more at:
https://www.w3.org/blog/2026/whats-new-in-the-w3c-design-system-september-2026/
#WebDesign #W3Csite

If you have ever tried to find out what a W3C group has been working on lately, you know it often means piecing together information from several sources: publication lists, GitHub repositories, mailing lists, meeting minutes, and more.

That's why our Systems Team has introduced activity pages: one place to see what a group has been doing, month by month.

They would like to hear what you use the pages for, and what you would want them to show next. See more at:
https://www.w3.org/blog/2026/introducing-group-activity-pages/

"We’re on a roll - EPUB 3.4 is coming" by @reidmore on the W3C blog

Wendy noted: "The Publishing Maintenance Working Group at W3C has been quietly working on yet another update for the EPUB3 standard, and we're excited to share what we have been up to. Our goal is to not only maintain the EPUB standard, but do our best to keep it in line with the needs of industry, and this update does exactly that."
Read more at:
https://www.w3.org/blog/2026/were-on-a-roll-epub-3-4-is-coming/
#EPUB3 #WebPublishing

Will you be at TPAC2026 in Dublin? Don’t miss the TPAC Hackathon there!

Everyone will be talking about it and you’re invited to be part of it! We have room for 30 people so register now!

Free for TPAC attendees
Solo or in pairs
All experience levels
Light dinner provided

Many thanks to @igalia, Digital Bazaar and Holopin who have made the Hackathon possible.
https://www.w3.org/register/tpac2026-hackathon

The Verifiable Credentials Working Group published a series of W3C Working Group Note Drafts for threat models. All identify and analyze security and privacy threats specific to their recommendation-track documents:
Recognized Entities Threat Model v1.0
Data Integrity Threat Model v1.1
Verifiable Credential Barcodes Threat Model v1.0
Verifiable Credentials Render Method Threat Model v1.0
VCALM Threat Model v1.0

See more at:
https://www.w3.org/news/2026/first-draft-notes-verifiable-credential-threat-models/
#VerifiableCredentials

Regulations limiting children’s access to online content have been broadly and rapidly deployed recently, which require that users provide assurance of their age. The consequences of these regulations may result in major changes to the web.

Tara Whalen and Amir Sharif are leading a mini-workshop to explore Age Assurance as part of #w3cTPAC in Dublin on 28 October.

The deadline for proposals has been extended to 8 October. See more at:
https://github.com/w3c/strategy/issues/569

W3C issues press release about developing Verifiable Credential Barcodes

Recently the data theft of approximately 160 million drivers licenses from the US and Canada was reported and unfortunately, identity thieves will use this data to impersonate victims.

Real-time revocation is needed to protect individuals against identity theft. W3C Verifiable Credential Barcodes are the solution to the future of physical document security. Read more at:
https://www.w3.org/news/2026/w3c-issues-press-release-about-developing-verifiable-credential-barcodes/

Are you interested in the positive and negative impacts of Generative AI on society and its intersection with W3C's Ethical Web Principles and Vision?

@tzviya, @hdv, and @christianliebel are organizing a mini-workshop on AI and Society in Dublin on 28 October as part of TPAC 2026.

Topics proposed include: AI and accessibility, the user and Agentic AI and enabled emissions. The deadline to submit proposals has been extended to 9 October. See more: https://github.com/w3c/strategy/issues/565
